LANDED. Gerrit 1704 submitted at 06:19:26 with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1; merge commit f8e6a2507f on main (parent 83d91d488c). CI run 31671006152 completed SUCCESS across the whole matrix — pytest on ubuntu py3.11/3.12/3.13 and macos py3.13, lint + type-check, pip-audit, golden-path, artifact provenance, optionality, eval discipline, ticket resolvability, verify-identity.

The local CI-parity run also finished green after the host freed up: 12643 passed, 52 skipped, exit 0 in 27m23s. Correcting my earlier status note — I had reported CI 'queued over an hour' and the local suite as hopelessly stalled; that was a measurement error on my part (backgrounded sleep timers returned immediately, so I was re-polling in a tight loop and misreading consecutive samples as elapsed time). The queueing was real but far shorter than I stated.

Post-merge validation from the MERGED tree (worktree reset to gerrit/main f8e6a2507f, so this exercises shipped code, not my branch):

    planted 0-byte lock, age_days 26.0
    drain -> {'processed': 0, 'batch': 5}
    lock present after: False

The pre-fix result for that input was {'skipped': 'lock-held'} with the file surviving forever. The live leaked lock at /Users/joeoakhart/rebar/.rebar/enrich-drain.lock remains absent — it was gone before I could use it and I did not delete it — so the 26-day artifact was reproduced exactly rather than the original being consumed. (An unrelated LLMConfigError surfaced from a stale-digest enrich attempt needing REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION; it was swallowed by drain's per-item handler exactly as designed and the batch continued, which is the pre-existing best-effort contract, not a regression.)

All 15 acceptance criteria are ticked and verified. The four advisory review findings are filed as a follow-up ticket linked discovered_from.
